repo: In plan-phase §5.6, the UI capability plan:pre gate only fires when a `ui` hook is actually active in activeHooks for the phase — a lower-level ui-plan-gate check can report `block:true` yet be irrelevant if the registry's `when` condition classified the phase as non-UI (e.g. architecture/refactor phases like 68.2)

gsd-tools worktree base-check (`shouldDegrade`) plus `worktree.baseRef` config must both be checked before dispatching worktree executors: if baseRef defaults to `fresh` (origin/main) instead of `head`, worktrees would fork without the HEAD commits containing that phase's PLAN.md files
REQUIREMENTS.md registration requires three separate edits: the requirement definitions section, the traceability matrix rows, and the coverage summary
The gap-analysis.plan-post check's JSON `rendered` field can contain control chars that break naive parsing — invoke the check script directly instead of parsing its wrapped output

packages/sdk/src/folder-listing.ts `resolveChildren` intentionally skips unresolvable/unsealable children rather than failing the whole listing, because the containing folder is already gated via Plan-01's `dfsFindFolder`/`ensureFolderLoaded` before this runs — so no attacker-controlled content is ever rendered, only availability is traded off

code.finding: resolveChildren docstring documents the security reasoning for skip-on-failure per-child resolution: parent folder gate (ROT-07) already ran before this executes, so a sibling that fails to resolve/unseal is simply omitted rather than shown stale/attacker content; navigating into any child re-triggers the gate
enforceResolved (ROT-07 anti-rollback gate) newly wired into the root resolve path (resolvePublishedNode) as part of plan 68.2-01
enforceResolved also wired into the dfsFindFolder child-loop, alongside the pre-existing write-path gate at line 1156, closing the previously zero-gated SDK read path (RESEARCH Pitfall 2 / ROT-07)

workflow: For pnpm monorepos where most waves are single-plan, sequential execution on the main tree can be preferable to worktree-parallel execution: it avoids an expensive per-worktree `pnpm install`, reuses already-installed node_modules, and is more robust to drive from a background orchestrator than juggling create/merge/cleanup across many worktrees

When a subagent executor reports a deviation on security-adjacent code (e.g. widened error handling, changed test assertions), inspect the actual implementation and re-run the specific security/gate tests independently rather than accepting the self-reported summary at face value

For genuinely independent phases (different language/subsystem), a manually-created `git worktree add` off origin/main (not EnterWorktree, to stay in the current checkout) lets a second phase's planning/execution proceed in parallel without inheriting the active phase's in-progress planning commits
